comments.content: Removing std::forward here changes the semantics from perfect forwarding to pass-by-value. If Args contains rvalue references, this will cause unnecessary copies. Should keep std::forward<Args>(args)... to preserve value categories.

The constructor initializes ed.m_source and ed.m_target to 0, but ed is a struct/class member. If edge_t has a constructor, this assignment in the body may be too late (after default construction). Prefer initializing ed in the member initializer list, e.g., WalkerEdge() : ed{0, 0} {} (adjusting for actual edge_t members). Also, v1, v2, idx already have in-class initializers {0}, so they are zero-initialized automatically.
